review.title: Enforce reviewer ownership of judgement gates
review.acceptance: Recording a judgement gate is mechanically restricted to the reviewer who is entitled to make it, so that the round-83 PW-0203 incident is REFUSED rather than merely retracted. THE DEFECT, MEASURED. ai:gate today checks three things: that the task is IN_PROGRESS or REVIEW, that it has an owner, and that any --agent assertion matches who the control plane believes is recording. It does not ask whether the gate being recorded is one the recorder is entitled to conclude. So on 2026-09-23 the implementation owner of PW-0203 ran `gate PW-0203 architecture-review pass --agent claude-media "PLACEHOLDER-NOT-RECORDED"` expecting a refusal, and the control plane wrote a passing judgement gate whose entire evidence was that placeholder string. Every judgement gate in this repository's history was in fact transcribed from a gpt-architect verdict, but that is a convention the machine does not enforce, and product invariant 8 is currently defended by discipline alone. REQUIRED: judgement gates are named as a class in configuration rather than hard-coded at the call site -- at minimum architecture-review, security-review and rights-review -- so a gate added later is classified deliberately rather than defaulting to self-recordable. REQUIRED: a judgement gate may be recorded only by the task's configured reviewAgent, or by another reviewer made explicitly authorized under an existing fallback policy; the implementation owner cannot self-record one, and the check must consider BOTH the owner and any asserted implementationAgent, on the same rule the self-approval check already applies. REQUIRED: executable implementation gates -- typecheck, unit, e2e, build, performance and their kin -- remain recordable by the implementation owner exactly as they are today, where policy permits. This task must not make the ordinary loop harder. REQUIRED: a placeholder evidence string does not become a valid judgement merely because the CLI syntax was accepted. State the rule the implementation adopts and defend it; a length floor alone is not it, since a long placeholder passes one. REQUIRED: an unauthorized attempt is refused BEFORE anything is written -- no task.gate entry, no gateResults mutation, no audit line that could later read as a recorded result. A refusal that writes first and retracts after is the mechanism this task exists to replace. REQUIRED: a regression in scripts/test-ai-control-plane.mjs reproduces the exact round-83 attempt -- the task's own owner recording architecture-review with a placeholder -- and asserts refusal plus an unchanged gateResults. REQUIRED: legitimate transcribed gpt-architect verdict recording REMAINS SUPPORTED. This is the load-bearing constraint, not an afterthought: the GitHub write integration returns 403, so every judgement gate in this project is presently recorded by Claude on the reviewer's behalf. An enforcement that makes transcription impossible stops the project. Make transcription explicit rather than implicit -- the implementer chooses the spelling; a flag that records the verdict's provenance is the obvious shape -- and say in the record that it was transcribed. REQUIRED: release and retraction remain available as audit-recovery mechanisms and are not the primary enforcement. REQUIRED: the round-83 incident history is NOT erased, rewritten or compacted. The gate.fabricated_result_retracted event, the release, the re-claim and the re-records stay exactly as they are; this task adds a refusal, it does not tidy a record.
review.notes: Created on gpt-architect's round-83 ruling, following the self-reported fabricated gate result on PW-0203. The reviewer independently checked the PW-0203 event history, accepted the recovery, and ruled the underlying control-plane defect open. Prioritised P0 on the reviewer's instruction that further PW reviews depend on judgement-gate provenance being mechanically trustworthy.

typecheck.evidence: EXECUTED on 47fc7cb. npm run typecheck at the root, own invocation, turbo 21/21, exit 0. npm run lint 11/11, zero problems and zero warnings. node -c on all three changed scripts. npm run ai:validate reports 101 tasks and 9 agents valid with only the two long-standing preferredAgent/lane warnings; npm run repo:validate passed; ai:sync regenerated the views cleanly. NOTE ON WHAT TYPECHECK MEANS FOR THIS TASK: the control plane is plain ESM JavaScript and is not in any tsconfig project, so tsc does not see scripts/ai-control-plane.mjs at all. The 21/21 is the workspaces' own typecheck, and it is reported here as the unchanged-baseline evidence it is rather than as a check of this task's code. What actually exercises this task's code is the unit gate.

unit.evidence: EXECUTED on 47fc7cb. node scripts/test-ai-control-plane.mjs -> 'AI control plane tests passed (71 scenarios).', exit 0. Monorepo npx turbo run test --force -> 20/20 packages, exit 0, apps/web at 1075 tests, every package unchanged. SCENARIO 10u IS THE NEW ONE AND IT REPRODUCES THE INCIDENT RATHER THAN DESCRIBING IT. Against a REAL git repository, because the placeholder rule resolves shas against an object database and a fixture that stubbed that would be testing the stub. Seven properties, each a distinct way this could have shipped as a fiction. (1) The exact round-83 command -- the task's own owner recording its reviewer's architecture-review with PLACEHOLDER-NOT-RECORDED -- is refused. (2) THE REFUSAL WRITES NOTHING: gateResults is serialised before and after and asserted byte-identical, so the guard is a guard and not a second retraction path. (3) Omitting --agent is refused, because recordedBy would fall back to task.owner and the self-record would happen with nobody having typed a name. (4) A task with no reviewAgent is refused with a message naming THAT as the defect, checked before the implementation-side rule so the owner is not sent looking for a permission that does not exist. (5) The placeholder rule is asserted three ways: a fluent 340-character review naming no commit is refused, a forty-hex token that resolves to nothing is refused -- the case a pattern test would have accepted and rev-parse does not -- and a real sha sitting beside the words 'Full rationale TBD' is refused by the substring net. (6) THE LEGITIMATE TRANSCRIBED PATH STILL WORKS, which is the load-bearing constraint: recorded as gpt-architect with --transcribed-by claude-lead, the result carries by=gpt-architect, transcribedBy=claude-lead and judgementCommitSha resolved to the full sha; a separate task asserts an ABBREVIATED sha resolves to the full one, because that is how reviewers actually write them, and that judgementCommitVerified is true inside a git repository. (7) Executable gates are untouched: the owner still records typecheck with no new arguments -- asserted FIRST so a version of this that made the ordinary loop harder fails there rather than at the end -- and --transcribed-by on an executable gate is refused rather than ignored, because an exit code is re-run and not relayed. One case is asserted honestly rather than flatteringly: a wholly unrelated agent attempting substitution is refused by the PRE-EXISTING ownership rule, which answers before the new authority check, and the scenario asserts that message and records in a comment that the authority check is defence in depth today and becomes the answering rule only if authorizedIndependentReviewers is populated -- at which point the ownership rule must be widened to match. TWO PRE-EXISTING DEFECTS THE ENFORCEMENT EXPOSED, both fixed rather than exempted. scripts/cloud/advance-completable.mjs recorded review-backed gates with no --agent, so the deterministic completion path was self-recording judgement gates under the implementer's name on every task it ever completed. And the regression suite's own implementToInProgress helper recorded architecture-review as the implementer, so the tests guarding this system were built on the defect; judgement gates now go through reviewWithJudgement, which records them as the reviewAgent after the task reaches REVIEW. ONE UNRELATED RED BUILD REPAIRED, and it was red on main before this task -- verified by stashing this work and re-running. Scenario 7 asserted PL-WV-0010 reaches READY_BUT_EXTERNAL because no locally executable agent advertised lane Recommendations; round 77 added Recommendations to claude-lead on the reviewer's own ruling, and the property silently became false. Per this file's standing rule the expectation was NOT retyped to match today's data: the fixture is now anchored to an executive agent's exclusive lane, which agentExecutable refuses unconditionally before adapters or capabilities, with an assertion that fails loudly if no such lane remains.

recommended.title: Production authentication and session resolution
recommended.acceptance: A request in a DEPLOYMENT can be identified, so that an account identity is never a typed header. This task owns the residual gpt-architect named when approving PW-0402, verbatim: PW-0402 does NOT establish production user authentication, and today a desktop build classifying as non-deployment would make the header the identity layer, with nothing currently preventing that classification. THE BOUNDARIES, WHICH THIS TASK DOES NOT MOVE. PW-0101 owns local listener authentication and hardening. PW-0402 owns authorization once an identity is known. PW-0401 owns the authenticated backend service for provider resolution. PW-0403 owns production account and session authentication and nothing else. REQUIRED: ADOPT the reviewed @liberty/auth/server Better Auth seam rather than replacing it. packages/auth/src/better-auth.ts is already the only module in the repository that imports better-auth, it already refuses a surface beyond ENABLED_AUTH_CAPABILITIES, and config.ts already validates secure-cookie, trusted-origin and baseURL behaviour. This task constructs the reviewed instance from that validated config; it does not stand up a second identity system beside it. REQUIRED: expose the Next App Router auth handler and endpoints, importing better-auth/next-js in apps/web rather than in the package, which must stay buildable and testable without Next -- the boundary better-auth.ts states in its own header. REQUIRED: a deployment request resolves AccountIdentity ONLY from a verified database-backed session. resolveRequestAccount gains a real deployment-authenticated branch instead of answering authentication_not_configured. REQUIRED: development headers stay strictly confined to a minted non-deployment runtime capability. The witness discipline in apps/web/src/lib/session/account.ts is preserved exactly -- a deployment cannot obtain an identity there, cannot be issued the witness, and a manufactured one is refused rather than accepted on the strength of its type. REQUIRED: a missing, malformed, expired or revoked session CANNOT produce an AccountIdentity. Each of the four is its own test, because 'expired' and 'revoked' fail through different code paths and a suite that covers only the missing case proves the least interesting one. REQUIRED: the desktop launch token cannot substitute for a user session. This is the exact confusion PW-0402's authorizeRoute was built to prevent by never being given a Request, and authentication must not reintroduce it from the other side. REQUIRED: a loopback origin cannot substitute for a user session. Being on 127.0.0.1 is not an identity. REQUIRED: profile selection stays ABOVE authentication and is not moved into Better Auth user or session product data. active_profile_selection is keyed by session in Liberty's own store, which is what lets the television and the phone act as different profiles; folding it into the identity library's session record would couple the two and lose that. REQUIRED: PW-0402's indistinguishable authorization refusal behaviour is preserved. An unauthenticated request and a request for another household's resource must not become distinguishable because one of them now fails earlier. REQUIRED: secure cookie, trusted-origin and baseURL behaviour comes from the existing validated auth configuration rather than from new literals at the handler. REQUIRED: no credential or secret is placed in the desktop artifact or in any log. REQUIRED: docs/SECURITY.md R4 is updated to state what is then true. Its current text was corrected in round 82 to say authorization is enforced and authentication is not; leaving that in place after this task ships would be a second competing truth.
recommended.notes: Filed in round 83 to own the residual gpt-architect named when approving PW-0402; acceptance rewritten in the same round to the reviewer's own round-83 specification, which is narrower and sharper than the original filing. allowedPaths gained apps/web/src/app/api/auth/** because Better Auth's validated basePath is /api/auth and the App Router handler has to live at the path the config already declares, not at a v1 path chosen to fit an earlier surface guess. The three packages/auth modules briefly added as reviewDependencies were removed again: packages/auth/src/** is already in allowedPaths and ai:validate correctly reported them redundant, because allowedPaths is always part of the reviewed surface.

recommended.title: The authenticated backend the desktop build talks to
recommended.acceptance: The counterparty the desktop forwarder already speaks to exists as a service instead of only as an e2e stub. docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 8 was ruled by the commander: provider resolution must not rely on the user-administered sidecar as its trust boundary, and the desktop build proxies to an authenticated backend. The FORWARDER is implemented and tested; the thing it forwards TO is e2e/src/backend-stub.mjs. REQUIRED: the same route contract, byte for byte -- the cross-target e2e suite already compares whole bodies between targets and must keep passing. REQUIRED: caller authentication, and a refusal that does not leak whether a content id exists. REQUIRED: provider credentials live only here, never in a desktop artifact, env var, config file or cached response; the build-target import-graph guard already proves the desktop bundle cannot reach @liberty/provider-sdk and this service is where that capability actually lives. REQUIRED: it is deployable and testable WITHOUT a licensed provider -- the resolution path must return an honest unavailable with provider_not_configured when none is wired, which is exactly what the web target already does. THIS TASK DOES NOT NEED CREDENTIALS and must not wait for them; PL-0302 remains the separate task that wires a real provider into it.
recommended.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict. SURFACE NOTE: this task's allowedPaths name directories that do not exist yet. The evidence-based narrowing procedure applies to reconciling work already in history; for genuinely new work the surface is the smallest set of paths the acceptance can be satisfied within, and it is narrowed again from the diff before review if it turns out to be wider than what was written.
